Ages 0-18 · Body · Mind · Money sense

What your child needs this year, laid out by age

Yanghaowa is a local-first parenting companion for parents of children aged 0 to 18. Add a child and three threads unfold for their current age band: physical health, emotional growth and money sense. Log the day in a tap, read a stage report, and talk a question through with Wenwen, the in-app assistant. No account, no server: every family record stays on your own phone.

What it does

Everything serves one loop: profile → age-staged content and logs → stage report → AI discussion.

Three threads that unfold by age band

Content is organised into 0-1, 1-3, 3-6, 6-12 and 12-18. No pocket money at age one, no brushing check-ins for a teenager. When a birthday moves the child into a new band, the whole app changes together.

Log today in one tap

Time outdoors, screen time, the family activity, brushing and today's mood sit on one home card. Height, expenses, reminders and wish goals each open a form in a single step. No streaks to keep.

Personality growth simulator

Drag six parenting sliders and a nine-axis radar updates in the same frame. Sliders start from your own parenting-style quiz, with dots from your real logs beside the radar. A trend simulation, not a prediction.

Wenwen: AI on your own key

The small companion in the corner asks about today's mood, surfaces reminders and discusses parenting questions. You configure the model key; by default only the age band and allowed summaries are sent, and you see the list first.

Reminders and family challenges

Vaccines are scheduled from the birthday; water and medicine ring on time and a tap lands on the right panel. Eye care, early bedtime and daily praise challenges run side by side with age-appropriate checklists.

Your data stays yours

A local snapshot every day, encrypted export files, and on iOS a copy in your own iCloud. Merge on import so a child is never duplicated; overwrite takes a snapshot first and can be undone for 24 hours.

One purchase, no subscription

The core is free. Pro unlocks the advanced features once, for life. Topic skill packs are small separate one-time purchases.

Frequently asked

Same text as the FAQ structured data; edit site.config.json first.

What is Yanghaowa?

A local-first parenting companion for parents of children aged 0 to 18. It follows three threads, physical health, emotional growth and money sense, by age band, from profile to age-staged content and logs, stage reports and AI discussion. Available on iOS and Android.

How is my data protected?

There is no account and no server of ours. Every record lives in a local database on your phone, and the app contains no analytics or ad SDK. The only network call is the AI request made with your own key, which by default sends the age band and trend summaries, with a card listing each item before it goes. Backup files are yours to keep, optionally passphrase-encrypted.

Is it paid? How does pricing work?

The download is free and the basics work: profiles, age-staged content, one-tap logging and reminders. Advanced features are unlocked by Pro, a one-time purchase that lasts for life, with no subscription and no ads. Topic skill packs are small separate one-time purchases that make the assistant sharper on that topic; they are not part of Pro and do not include model costs. Prices are shown in your local store, and "Restore purchases" brings everything back on a new phone.

What does the AI need, and what does it send?

You enter an API key from a model provider in the app; usage is billed between you and that provider. Requests include only the child's age band and trend summaries within scopes you allow, such as growth percentile ranges, habit check-in days and task completion rates; never names, birthdays or exact measurements, and money data is off by default. Each scope has its own switch, and a card lists every injected item before sending.

How do I move my data to a new phone?

Export a backup from "Me → Data & backup" (the encrypted version needs a passphrase), send the file to the new phone and choose "Restore from backup → Choose a file" on the same page there. On iOS with iCloud private backup on, a new device on the same Apple ID can pick "Backup in iCloud" directly. Import offers merge or overwrite; merge never duplicates a child, and a snapshot is taken before overwrite so you can undo within 24 hours.
